Imported from `@qlivedev/qlive-ts/vite`, not from the package's main entry.

## trackUsage()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function trackUsage(options?: TrackUsagePluginOptions): Plugin;
```

The Vite plugin that records the calls QLive's server-side analysis reads -- which query a view
injects, which paths declared `noSchema()` -- plus any the application adds through `trackedFunctions`.

`vite build` writes the analysis to `track-usage.json` in the output directory, where the backend reads
it. The dev server keeps it in memory and pushes each change to `backendOrigin`, and while it runs it
also rewrites the result type of every saved `GraphQLQuery` to follow its query (see `queryTypes`).

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `options` | where to analyze, what to track and where the backend is  |

**Returns** the plugin, for `plugins` in `vite.config.ts`

## TrackUsagePluginOptions

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface TrackUsagePluginOptions
```

Options of `trackUsage`. All of them are optional; an application usually sets
`backendOrigin` and nothing else.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.trackedFunctions

```ts
trackedFunctions?: Record<string, TrackedFunctionSpec>;
```

Calls to record on top of `QLIVE_TRACKED_FUNCTIONS`. Their keys have to be the application's
own: one of QLive's is refused rather than merged over, because the server reads the framework's
calls back out under exactly those names.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.sourceRoot

```ts
sourceRoot?: string;
```

Absolute path to the directory tracking is scoped to. Default: `src/` below Vite's `root`, which is
where an application's own code lives.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.debug

```ts
debug?: boolean;
```

Logs to the console every call the analysis matches and every value it records or fails to
evaluate. For finding out why a call is missing from the analysis. Default: false.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.indexes

```ts
indexes?: boolean;
```

Records the source offsets ([start, end]) of every tracked call alongside its arguments. Consumers that
rewrite the source at the call site (the QLive backend patches the result type into every
`new GraphQLQuery<...>()`) cannot work without them, so leave this on unless you only need the
argument values.

Default: true.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.seedFile

```ts
seedFile?: string;
```

Previously-built track-usage.json used to pre-seed dev mode. Default: `dist/` next to `sourceRoot`,
under `outputFileName`.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.outputFileName

```ts
outputFileName?: string;
```

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.backendOrigin

```ts
backendOrigin?: string;
```

Origin of the QLive backend, e.g. "http://localhost:8080". Live track-usage data gets POSTed there as
it changes. `vite build` writes track-usage.json to disk for the backend to read, but `vite dev` never
touches disk, so this is dev mode's only way to get fresh data to a backend that needs it live (e.g.
for codegen). Omit to skip pushing entirely.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.pushDebounceMs

```ts
pushDebounceMs?: number;
```

How long to collect changed modules before pushing them to `backendOrigin`, in milliseconds. One save
can transform several modules, and the backend regenerates types for every module it is handed, so
they are worth sending as one push. Default: 200.

### TrackUsagePluginOptions.queryTypes

```ts
queryTypes?: QueryTypeOptions | false;
```

How the query result types are generated. While a dev server runs, every saved query gets its
`GraphQLQuery<T>` rewritten, so the type next to a query follows the query.

Left out, the types are generated whenever `schema.graphql` is next to the Vite config and
`@qlivedev/qlive-codegen` is installed. Given, its schema has to exist -- silence would look
like a plugin that does not work. `false` turns the generation off.

## QueryTypeOptions

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface QueryTypeOptions
```

Where the query result types come from and what they import, for
`TrackUsagePluginOptions.queryTypes`.

### QueryTypeOptions.schema

```ts
schema?: string;
```

### QueryTypeOptions.typesModule

```ts
typesModule?: string;
```

Module the generated domain types live in, relative to `sourceRoot` and without extension. It is
what a generated result type picks its fields out of, and what the query module gets an import of.
Default: "types", i.e. what `generate-ts` writes to `src/types.d.ts`.

## QLIVE_TRACKED_FUNCTIONS

<span class="api-kind">constant</span>

```ts
declare const QLIVE_TRACKED_FUNCTIONS: Record<string, TrackedFunctionSpec>;
```

The calls QLive's own analysis is built on. Their keys are the symbolic names the server looks up a call under --
ModuleFunctionReferences.USE_INJECTION_CALL_NAME and its neighbours name the same strings
on the Java side -- so what belongs in here is the framework's to state and not an application's to
get right. An application adds its own entries through `trackedFunctions`, and is refused a key that
is already one of these.

## TrackedFunctionSpec

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface TrackedFunctionSpec
```

Which calls the analysis records: calls of `fn` on whatever `module` exports, or of the module
itself when `fn` is empty. Only statically evaluable arguments are recorded, unless the options
below loosen that.

### TrackedFunctionSpec.module

```ts
module: string;
```

### TrackedFunctionSpec.fn

```ts
fn: string;
```

### TrackedFunctionSpec.varArgs

```ts
varArgs?: boolean | number;
```

Enables varargs support where a function can have n static arguments and then a number of variable arguments
that have no restriction on being static. If varargs is a number, it defines how many arguments are statically
captured (true is the same as 1)

### TrackedFunctionSpec.captureContext

```ts
captureContext?: boolean;
```

Allows recording context expressions against the matched location in the AST. e.g. "parent.id.name"

### TrackedFunctionSpec.allowIdentifier

```ts
allowIdentifier?: boolean;
```

Enables identifier matching where instead of a static expression, we capture the *name* of an identifier to
reference some global namespace (or local in some way).

## analyzeSourceTree()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function analyzeSourceTree(options: AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions): TrackUsageAnalysis;
```

Runs the track-usage analysis over a whole source tree in one go, outside of Vite.

The plugin gets its analysis handed to it file by file, as Vite transforms them, which is the wrong
shape for a tool that is not a dev server -- the codegen CLI wants the whole tree before it starts.
Both go through the same babel pass, so what a build-time generator sees is what the dev-time one
sees: the same recorded calls under the same names, at the same source offsets.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `options` | what to analyze and how  |

**Returns** the analysis of every tracked file below `sourceRoot`

## AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions
```

Options of `analyzeSourceTree`: the plugin's options minus everything that only makes sense
inside a running Vite.

### AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions.sourceRoot

```ts
sourceRoot: string;
```

### AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions.trackedFunctions

```ts
trackedFunctions?: Record<string, TrackedFunctionSpec>;
```

### AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions.debug

```ts
debug?: boolean;
```

### AnalyzeSourceTreeOptions.indexes

```ts
indexes?: boolean;
```

## TrackUsageAnalysis

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface TrackUsageAnalysis
```

The analysis of one source tree, as `babel-plugin-track-usage` records it. Keyed by module id
relative to `sourceRoot` ("./app/Q_Foo"), which is how the backend addresses a module as well.

### TrackUsageAnalysis.usages

```ts
usages: Record<string, unknown>;
```
